notes: Stitcher, much faster on large libraries. Stitching: several groups are now joined at the same time (new setting 'Joins at once' under Performance, 4 on this PC), and when the sound has to be matched to the picture, that is done for several clips at once ('Sounds re-synced at once'). Each joined file is made exactly as before.

Sound bitrate 'Automatic' now follows the sound (on every page): normal sound gets 96 kbps per channel as before, low-rate sound gets what it can use - the 8 kHz sound of security cameras 32 kbps. Asked for 96, the encoder could not use it (the file came out the same size) but took four times as long. A bitrate you pick yourself is used as it is.

Stitcher scan: every clip is read once and remembered, so stitching no longer reads them all again and a second scan of the same folder takes seconds. The scene pictures are taken with one start of FFmpeg per clip instead of two, and are kept in a small database instead of one big file that was written again and again (the pictures already made are taken over). Regrouping after you change a setting is quick.

Stitcher: with 'Compare scenes' and 'Keep different cameras apart' both unticked, a scan no longer takes scene pictures at all - that is the slowest part of a scan. Tick either one and scan again to get them back.
